before.label: Black history
before.date_label: 1800s roots · ASNLH founded 1915 · Black Reconstruction 1935 · later expansion
before.description: Challenges racist historical narratives and recovers Black agency, institutions, and political struggle. Abolitionism, community scholarship, and Black institutions provide independent roots, not merely applications of European theory.
before.representative_figures_and_works: William Wells Brown; George Washington Williams (1882–83); Carter G. Woodson; W. E. B. Du Bois, Black Reconstruction (1935). Carter G. Woodson and colleagues founded the Association for the Study of Negro Life and History (now ASALH) in 1915. Postwar and later examples include John Hope Franklin, From Slavery to Freedom (1947), and Darlene Clark Hine, Black Women in White (1989).

representative_people.context: Postwar synthesis placing African American history within the interpretation of United States history.

representative_people.works: “African-American Women’s History and the Metalanguage of Race” (1992); Righteous Discontent (1993)

representative_people.context: Her NCNW cooperates with WCWA after she declines the proposed committee chair; Black women’s preservation work exceeds this short-lived collaboration.

before.scope_note: Independent scholarship, community education, publishing and collecting precede later academic recognition. Biography, national synthesis and Black women’s history pursue different questions. This selection remains weighted toward African American scholarship; diaspora links do not make all Black histories one national tradition.

finding: Retain the inclusive Black history field label and show coverage through 2000. The previous selected milestone 1935 visually implied an early endpoint despite later-expansion wording. Existing roster already includes postwar and late-twentieth-century scholarship.
date_basis: 2000 is the graph’s existing main_period coverage boundary, not a new publication date, an assertion of exhaustive coverage, or the end of Black history.

validation.preservation: Only Black history date_label changed; all other existing graph content exact. All 109 date labels remain chronological.
validation.build: Exactly six allowlisted public files, all byte-identical to inputs.
validation.tests: 14 Python and 8 JavaScript data tests passed in immediately preceding revision 1.103; this single-label follow-up checked with structural validation, exact preservation and build verification.
